# Sirach Chapter 40 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 40 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_040_page_001.jpg

---

40:1 Great hardship has been created for every human being, and a heavy yoke is upon the sons of Adam from the day of their coming forth from their mother's womb until the day they return to the mother of all things.

40:2 Their thoughts, and fear of heart, and their imagination of things to come, and the day of their death —

40:3 from the one who sits on a glorious throne to the one who is humbled in earth and ashes,

40:4 from the one who wears purple and a crown to the one who is clothed in burlap —

40:5 wrath and envy and trouble and agitation and fear of death and fury and strife. And when one lies on his bed to rest, his sleep at night alters his knowledge.

40:6 Little or none is his rest, and in sleep as in a day's watch he is troubled in his heart: sometimes the terror of a dream, sometimes he falls into deep sleep, and a little rest in his slumber — as it were, a rescue from the day of battle.

40:7 He rouses himself and marvels that the terror was nothing at all.

40:8 Such things happen to all creatures, human beings and animals, but for sinners seven times more.

40:9 Death and bloodshed and strife and sword, calamities, famine and ruin and plague —

40:10 all these were created for the wicked, and it is because of them that the Flood came.

40:11 All things that are from the earth return to the earth, and what is from the waters returns to the sea.

40:12 All bribery and injustice will be wiped out, but good faith will stand forever.

40:13 The wealth of the unjust will dry up like a torrent, and will crash like the sound of a mighty thunderstorm.

40:14 A generous man will be gladdened, but transgressors will utterly fail.

40:15 The children of the ungodly will not put out many branches, and impure roots stand on rocky ground.

40:16 The reed by every body of water and river bank will be uprooted before all grass.

40:17 Kindness is like a paradise of blessings, and charitable giving endures forever.

40:18 The life of a laborer who is self-sufficient is sweet, but better than both is the one who finds treasure.

40:19 Children and the building of a city establish a name, but better than both is the one who finds wisdom. Cattle and orchards make men flourish, but better than both is a beloved wife.

40:20 Wine and music gladden the heart, but better than both is the love of wisdom.

40:21 The flute and the harp make melody, but better than both is a pleasant voice.

40:22 The eye desires grace and beauty, but better than both are the green shoots of grain.

40:23 A friend and companion are opportune at the right time, but better than both is a wife with a husband.

40:24 Brothers and help are for a time of trouble, but charitable giving rescues better than both.

40:25 Gold and silver make one's footing secure, but better than both is counsel.

40:26 Riches and strength lift up the heart, but better than both is the fear of the Lord. There is no want in the fear of the Lord, and there is no need to seek further help.

40:27 The fear of the Lord is a paradise of blessing, and they cover him with more glory than any covering.

40:28 My son, do not lead the life of a beggar; it is better to die than to beg.

40:29 When one looks to the table of another, one's life cannot be considered a life. One pollutes the soul with another man's food, but the intelligent and well-instructed man guards against that.

40:30 In the mouth of the shameless, begging is sweet, but in his stomach a fire is kindled.
